method: Original summaries independently checked against named publisher, author or catalogue sources and exact selected edition identities. Work content evidence is distinguished from edition-specific claims. No source excerpt or private Search Console data is published.

entries.title: Harry Potter en de Orde van de Feniks
entries.author: J. K. Rowling
entries.text: Tijdens zijn zomervakantie bij de Duffelingen voelt Harry zich steeds meer buitengesloten. Ook zijn vrienden laten weinig van zich horen, terwijl hij juist naar Zweinstein terug wil. Een onverwachte wending brengt zelfs zijn toelating tot het vijfde schooljaar in gevaar. Harry probeert te begrijpen wat er om hem heen gebeurt, maar nieuwe ontdekkingen maken dat steeds moeilijker. Dit vijfde avontuur begint met onzekerheid over de plek waar hij zich thuis dacht te voelen.

evidence.basis: De uitgever bevestigt de exacte Nederlandse paperback met ISBN 9789061697008, auteur J.K. Rowling en vertaler Wiebe Buddingh’. De flapbeschrijving noemt de zomer bij de Duffelingen, de afwezige vrienden, Harry's wens terug te keren en onzekerheid over zijn vijfde schooljaar.

entries.identityNotes: Bewaar de spaties in de opgeslagen auteursnaam J. K. Rowling voor de editiecontrole. De uitgever schrijft J.K. Rowling; titel en exact ISBN bevestigen dezelfde Nederlandse paperback.

entries.title: Threshing Day
entries.author: Rebecca Yarros
entries.text: Thirteen stories return to the Empyrean world and the dangerous trial in which Basgiath cadets seek a dragon's bond. The collection follows characters including Xaden Riorson, Rhiannon Matthias and Liam Mairi as competition with other would-be riders meets the dragons' own choices. It expands the series through their experiences of Threshing. This deluxe hardcover includes sixteen colour illustrations by Joe Requeza. Because the stories contain spoilers, the publisher recommends reading the collection after Onyx Storm.

evidence.basis: Publisher confirms exact ISBN 9780349450612 as the limited deluxe hardcover, thirteen stories, Basgiath dragon-bonding trial, named characters, sixteen full-colour illustrations by Joe Requeza and suggested reading after Onyx Storm because of spoilers.
Official FAQ distinguishes deluxe hardcover ISBN 9780349450612 from standard hardcover ISBN 9780349451428.

entries.identityNotes: The saved title is Threshing Day. Exact publisher ISBN resolves the former placeholder URL to Threshing Day (Limited Deluxe Edition), a thirteen-story companion collection. Do not describe it as book four or invent a continuation of Violet's main storyline.

entries.title: Hunter × Hunter, Volume 1
entries.author: 冨樫義博
entries.text: Gon leaves his rural home determined to become a Hunter, the profession his father followed. His voyage brings him together with Leorio and Kurapika, two other hopeful applicants. Reaching the Hunter Exam is already a challenge: before they can enter the examination hall, the travellers must prove themselves through a series of tests. This opening manga volume introduces Gon's ambition and his new companions as they discover how dangerous the path to becoming a Hunter can be.

evidence.basis: VIZ confirms volume one, story and art by Yoshihiro Togashi, and exact paperback ISBN 9781591167532. Its synopsis establishes Gon's ambition, Leorio and Kurapika, the sea journey and tests before the Exam Hall.

entries.identityNotes: The saved LumiScore identity uses the author's Japanese name 冨樫義博; the publisher uses Yoshihiro Togashi. Preserve the exact saved author and title for the guard. VIZ's 'Hunter x Hunter, Vol. 1' is the same exact-ISBN edition.

entries.title: Outline
entries.author: Rachel Cusk
entries.text: A novelist travels to Athens to teach a writing course and listens closely to the people she meets during her visit. A fellow passenger, students and other writers tell her about their relationships, disappointments and ambitions. Across ten conversations, their accounts gradually reveal something of the woman listening, including the loss she is learning to face. Rachel Cusk builds the story through these encounters, examining how people shape their lives into narratives and what those narratives leave unspoken.

evidence.basis: Publisher book-details paragraph confirms the novelist teaching in Athens, ten conversations, fellow passenger, students and other writers, and the listening narrator confronting loss. The publisher identifies the first Outline trilogy volume. This live paperback page is a different ISBN; shared novel content only is used.

Vermont State Colleges Libraries catalog confirms Rachel Cusk, Outline, first American edition, Farrar Straus and Giroux, English, exact ISBN 9780374228347. Its description independently agrees on the ten-conversation structure and Athens setting.

Spokane Public Library MARC record independently lists 9780374228347 as the hardback, Rachel Cusk, first American edition and English. This prevents attributing the paperback source’s ISBN/format to the selected edition.

entries.identityNotes: The public attribution links to the publisher’s available paperback page for the same novel. Exact selected hardcover ISBN is independently catalog-confirmed. No format-specific or page-count claim appears in the summary. Independent review corrected the duration wording: the publisher excerpt describes a short visit, not an entire summer.

entries.title: As Long as the Lemon Trees Grow
entries.author: Zoulfa Katouh
entries.text: The Syrian revolution changes Salama Kassab's life from pharmacy studies to caring for wounded people in a hospital in Homs. Her pregnant friend Layla is among those she wants to protect, while a hallucination called Khawf urges her to escape. Meeting Kenan complicates the choice between leaving and staying. Zoulfa Katouh's novel follows Salama as love, grief and responsibility pull her in different directions. This paperback edition also includes Joy, a short story featuring Salama and Kenan.

evidence.basis: Publisher confirms exact paperback ISBN, author, Salama's hospital work, pregnant Layla, Khawf as a hallucination, Kenan and the included bonus story Joy.
Publisher's educational resource confirms Salama was a pharmacy student and volunteers in a hospital in Homs, with leaving Syria versus staying central to her predicament.

entries.identityNotes: The saved title includes 'the': As Long as the Lemon Trees Grow. Exact ISBN identifies the Bloomsbury paperback containing Joy; no audiobook or different-edition details are applied.

entries.title: Season of Migration to the North
entries.author: al-Ṭayyib Ṣāliḥ
entries.text: After studying in Europe, a young Sudanese man returns to his village beside the Nile and encounters Mustafa Sa'eed, whose past includes a life in London. Mustafa's account of his career and destructive relationships unsettles the narrator's ideas about home and belonging. As their lives become entangled, Tayeb Salih explores the lingering influence of colonialism, expectations placed on men and women, and the uneasy relationship between a community and those who leave it.

evidence.basis: Publisher identifies Season of Migration to the North, Tayeb Salih, translator Denys Johnson-Davies and exact ISBN 9780894101991. Its work description confirms the Sudanese student, London and destructive cross-cultural relationships. No review praise, awards or disputed first-publication date used.

Publisher description for another English edition of the same Denys Johnson-Davies translation confirms the narrator returning to his Nile village, Mustafa Sa’eed’s London history, the aftermath of colonial rule, and tensions involving Europe/Africa and men/women. Used for shared work content only; its introduction and ISBN are not attributed to the selected edition.

National Tsing Hua University library bibliography links exact ISBN 9780894101991 with the catalog author form Salih, al-Tayyib and the English title, supporting the difference between the live transliteration and the publisher’s Tayeb Salih form.

entries.identityNotes: Keep the exact current author guard al-Ṭayyib Ṣāliḥ from the selected public edition. Publisher uses Tayeb Salih. ISBN and library authority form corroborate identity; do not broaden the match to other ISBNs.

entries.title: On Bullshit
entries.author: Harry G. Frankfurt
entries.sourceName: Princeton University Press — The University Press Group catalogue
entries.text: Harry G. Frankfurt examines a kind of speech that aims to make an impression without taking responsibility for whether its claims are true. He distinguishes this indifference from a lie, which depends on recognizing the truth and deliberately concealing it. The essay asks what people are doing when they speak this way, why it is common, and how repeated disregard for accuracy can weaken a person's relationship with truth.

evidence.basis: Official University Press Group Philosophy Spring/Summer 2024 catalogue, printed page 19 / PDF page 20, identifies Princeton University Press, Harry G. Frankfurt, On Bullshit and exact ISBN 9780691122946. Description explains the distinction from lying, indifference to truth, impression management and the potential effect of repeated use. Quotes, praise and sales claims are excluded.
Princeton’s own Fall 2023 backlist catalogue confirms title, author and exact ISBN 9780691122946. Used for bibliographic identity only.
NII/CiNii catalog independently confirms exact ISBN, author, English language and Princeton University Press. Identifies the text as an essay originally published in Raritan.

entries.identityNotes: Exact ISBN belongs to the original Princeton book, not the later anniversary ISBN. No anniversary postscript, format, pagination or new-edition claim is included. Public source is the accessible official distributor catalogue because the publisher product page was inaccessible in the web tool.

entries.title: Boy-Crazy Stacey (The Baby-Sitters Club #8)
entries.author: Ann M. Martin
entries.text: Stacey and Mary Anne accompany the Pike family to the New Jersey shore for a fortnight of babysitting. The trip takes a different direction when Stacey falls for Scott, a lifeguard who is older than she is. Mary Anne worries that her friend's hopes will end in disappointment, but finding a way to tell her is difficult. The eighth Baby-Sitters Club novel places a summer crush alongside the demands of friendship and looking after children.

evidence.basis: Publisher's original-novel book list confirms Pike family, two-week Jersey Shore trip, Stacey and Mary Anne helping out, the older lifeguard Scott and Mary Anne's concern for Stacey. This is the prose series page, not the graphic adaptation.
Bibliographic verification only: exact ISBN 9780590435093, author Ann M. Martin, English Scholastic edition and series number eight. No Open Library description reused.

entries.identityNotes: Preserve the original prose series designation #8. The later graphic adaptation has a different series number and ISBN and is not the selected edition.

entries.title: The Time of the Doves (La Plaza del Diamante)
entries.author: Mercè Rodoreda
entries.text: Natalia, a shop worker, finds her everyday life overtaken by war and loss. After her husband's death, she must care for two young children while holding on to memories of their marriage, with its mixture of happiness and hardship. Mercè Rodoreda follows her efforts to survive the Spanish Civil War and its aftermath, showing political upheaval through the experiences of a woman trying to keep her family alive.

evidence.basis: Graywolf’s official title page identifies Mercè Rodoreda, translator David Rosenthal, exact ISBN 9780915308750 and the English edition. Its publisher description confirms a shop worker living through the Spanish Civil War and beyond. No review blurbs are used.

WorldCat catalog for Graywolf’s 1986 English edition summarizes Natalia caring for two young children after her husband’s death while remembering the happiness and hardship of their marriage. Search retrieval returned the catalog summary; direct open returned cache miss.
Google Books independently identifies the Graywolf English edition, Mercè Rodoreda, October 1986 and matching title. Supports edition identity alongside the exact-ISBN publisher page.

entries.identityNotes: Keep exact selected title The Time of the Doves (La Plaza del Diamante). Publisher uses the shorter English title; exact ISBN identifies the same edition. Do not silently switch to another English translation or change the catalog title guard.

entries.title: Repatriated
entries.author: Adriaan Van Dis
entries.text: In a seaside town in the Netherlands, a boy grows up under the influence of his father's fears. Mr Java, scarred by war and colonial experience, prepares his son for disasters he believes are approaching, from spying to nuclear attack. The boy's mother and three half-sisters respond to his father's obsessions with scepticism. Adriaan van Dis follows the son's attempt to gain independence while his family's experiences in Indonesia continue to shape life at home.

evidence.basis: Official Penguin/William Heinemann page identifies Repatriated by Adriaan Van Dis and confirms the Dutch seaside setting, Mr Java’s wartime and colonial background, his nuclear/spying fears, son, wife and her three daughters from a previous marriage in Indonesia. This later paperback supplies shared work content, not selected-edition format or pagination.

Google Books identifies Repatriated: A Novel in Sixty Scenes, Adriaan Dis, translator David Colmer, Penguin Random House 2008 and exact ISBN 0434011800 / 9780434011803. Publisher description agrees on Mr Java and the family plot.
Independent exact-ISBN identity corroboration: Repatriated, Adriaan van Dis, Random House, English, 9780434011803. Plot agrees with the official publisher. Retailer ratings and opinions are not used.

entries.identityNotes: Keep live author Adriaan Van Dis as the exact guard. Do not infer work identity from Goodreads’ combined editions list, which mixes this title with My Father’s War/Indische duinen. This summary is tied to the exact Repatriated ISBN and its own publisher description.

entries.title: This Lie Will Kill You
entries.author: Chelsea Pitcher
entries.sourceName: Margaret K. McElderry Books / Simon & Schuster
entries.text: Five teenagers arrive at a remote mansion believing they have a chance to win fifty thousand dollars. What connects them is a party a year earlier, when someone died and each of them concealed part of what happened. Their invitation is a trap arranged by someone seeking revenge. Chelsea Pitcher's thriller brings the survivors together under pressure to account for that night, making their conflicting secrets central to both the mystery and their chances of getting out alive.

evidence.basis: Official exact-ISBN e-book page confirms author, five teenagers, the earlier fatal party, isolated mansion, supposed $50,000 contest and a revenge plot aimed at revealing the truth.

entries.identityNotes: ISBN 9781534443266 identifies the English e-book. The paperback and hardcover have different ISBNs; no print-specific features are attributed to this edition.

entries.title: Personal Memoirs of U. S. Grant
entries.author: Ulysses S. Grant
entries.sourceName: Ulysses S. Grant via Project Gutenberg
entries.text: Ulysses S. Grant looks back on military life and the decisions made during the American Civil War. He describes campaigns from a commander's perspective, paying attention to terrain, supplies and relationships between officers as well as events on the battlefield. His recollections place personal experience beside arguments about the causes and conduct of war. The account presents his own judgments about the people, choices and responsibilities involved.

evidence.basis: Primary text of Grant’s own memoir. Preface explicitly distinguishes his personal comments and viewpoint; chapter contents and text cover military campaigns, transportation/supply, commanders and political causes of war. Summary is original prose based on the memoir itself, not Gutenberg’s automatically generated landing-page summary.

Bibliographic identity only: catalog edition OL11826674M confirms exact title Personal Memoirs of U. S. Grant, author Ulysses S. Grant, publisher IndyPublish.com, January 2006 and ISBN 9781421934679 / 1421934671. Its community/work description is not used.

Secondary corroboration only: the exact ISBN is listed as an English IndyPublish paperback by Ulysses S. Grant. Does not establish the completeness or volume arrangement of the selected edition; no rating or review is used.

entries.identityNotes: Exact selected ISBN/title/author match the bibliographic record. A surviving primary IndyPublish edition page was not found, and the record does not reliably establish completeness or volume arrangement. Summary deliberately describes the military memoir at work level and makes no assertion that this ISBN includes both volumes, all chapters, a particular pagination, supplementary letters or presidency coverage.

entries.title: Come as You Are
entries.author: Amy J. Fetzer
entries.sourceName: Digital Downloads Ohio / OverDrive — Kensington Books catalogue
entries.text: A covert assignment in Venezuela brings Logan Chambliss and the Dragon One team close to death. His situation becomes more complicated when Tessa Carlyle reappears, although he believed her dead. Tessa, a location scout working in Fiji, has been forced by blackmail into helping someone from her past. As their paths converge, old feelings become tangled with deception and danger. This romantic suspense novel follows the pair through a mission whose consequences extend beyond their own survival.

evidence.basis: Official library lending catalogue supplies Kensington Books' work description, naming Logan Chambliss, Dragon One, Tessa Carlyle, Fiji, blackmail and the Venezuela mission. It identifies the English e-book of the same work, ISBN 9780758283276.
Publisher's author catalogue independently confirms Come As You Are as a book by Amy J. Fetzer and links the e-book edition.
Edition identity only: publisher-supplied distributor listing explicitly maps print ISBN 9780758216571 to e-book ISBN 9780758283276 under Amy J. Fetzer and Brava.
Additional bibliographic check: selected paperback ISBN 9780758216571, Amy J. Fetzer, Kensington, English and December 2007. This retailer is not the primary source for the original paraphrase.

entries.identityNotes: This is Amy J. Fetzer's romantic suspense novel, not Emily Nagoski's nonfiction title. Primary work description is available through the licensed library catalogue; Kensington's author page confirms the work, but its linked product page could not be fetched. Print-to-e-book identity is explicitly mapped by the distributor; no e-book-specific features are claimed for the selected paperback.

entries.title: Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban
entries.author: J. K. Rowling
entries.text: Harry's third year at Hogwarts begins under the shadow of Sirius Black's escape from Azkaban. He is warned that the fugitive may be looking for him, while Dementors guard the school and make the threat feel close. With Ron and Hermione, Harry follows clues that connect the danger to his family's past. This third Harry Potter story turns assumptions about guilt and loyalty into a mystery whose answers change his understanding of the people around him.

evidence.basis: Official Wizarding World book guide, retrieved through indexed search text, supports Sirius's escape, the warning that he is pursuing Harry, the school setting and Dementors. Direct text extraction only returned the site's shell.

Official story commentary explains why the previous description's assertion that Sirius murdered Harry's parents is wrong. The new text preserves the mystery without giving that false statement or revealing the resolution.

Library's own catalogue search text identifies the English Thorndike Press large-print edition, J. K. Rowling and exact ISBN 9780786222742. Direct open returned 403. Use for edition identity only, not its broad plot wording.

entries.identityNotes: Exact live edition, not the more common Scholastic ISBN. Replaces a factual error and unrendered Markdown in the upstream description. Does not change catalogue identity or publication year.

entries.title: The Death of Truth [Hardcover] Michiko Kakutani
entries.author: michiko kakutani
entries.text: Writing in the context of American politics in 2018, Michiko Kakutani examines how public debate can lose its commitment to shared facts. She connects political rhetoric with developments in media, technology and intellectual life, drawing on writers including George Orwell and Hannah Arendt. Her argument considers propaganda, conspiracy theories and the tendency to favour beliefs that confirm what people already think. The book is a work of cultural and political criticism about the conditions that make falsehood persuasive.

evidence.basis: Publisher work description supports the argument, fields discussed, named writers and 2018 original publication. It is evidence for the work's contents, not for the selected William Collins ISBN. Political claims are described as Kakutani's argument in its publication context.

Indexed Spanish government library procurement catalogue lists exact ISBN 9780008312787, The Death of Truth, Michiko Kakutani, William Collins, London, 2018. Direct PDF open now returned 404; indexed record corroborated with two current retailer edition records.
Exact ISBN, English, title, author, William Collins and 2018 corroborate edition identity.
Exact ISBN 9780008312787 and hardcover title The Death of Truth by Michiko Kakutani corroborate removal of the imported retailer format/author suffix from the display title.

entries.identityNotes: Guard uses the exact selected raw edition title and author spelling. A separate exact-edition display correction shows The Death of Truth and Michiko Kakutani while preserving raw editionTitle for source bindings. No generic title stripping or edition reassignment.
